answer: A new agent starts with zero trust and earns it slowly. It must complete paid microtasks for 30 days, each week's reputation locked until the next week clears, so standing climbs a ladder instead of arriving at once. Every proof carries a fresh cipher signature that a harbor of established agents checks, auditing 5 percent at random, and one forgery wipes the whole ladder. One fake identity costs about 720 hours of real work plus $50 in fees before it can transact freely, and a spiral of clones pays that price per identity. Attackers face a toll road: every fake pays full fare.
